_about: Example curated stream splits. Every split defines a CUT GEOMETRY (a line or a polygon boundary) that slices the channels it crosses. from_dict ignores _comment/_about. See splits.schema.md.

splits._comment: PRIMARY FORM: a coordinate + a target mainstem (blk). Builds a short cut LINE perpendicular to that blue line at the nearest point, then cuts it. Use for a hand-picked spot on one channel.
splits.label: Squilax bridge

splits._comment: BRAIDED RIVER: a coordinate + a WSC target. The perpendicular cut line spans proximity_m, so it slices the main channel AND every side channel of that WSC it crosses within range (and nothing far away). This is how a section boundary crosses a braided river cleanly.
splits.label: section boundary

splits._comment: EXPLICIT LINE: author the cut line yourself (>=2 coords). Cuts every eligible channel it crosses. Use when a perpendicular auto-line is awkward.
splits.label: custom cut

splits._comment: LAKE: cut at the lake polygon boundary. Produces 'upstream of Adams Lake' / 'downstream of Adams Lake'.
splits.label: Adams Lake

splits._comment: MU BOUNDARY: needs BOTH management units; the cut is the shared boundary LINE between mu_a and mu_b. Curated only where specific regs differ across the boundary.
splits.label: Zone 2 / Zone 3

splits._comment: CONFLUENCE: cut where a tributary (by BLK, not name) meets the target mainstem — robust to unnamed tributaries and tributaries entering in multiple places.
splits.label: the confluence
